customer.business: Winner Takes All — tournament software a venue pays for, to run its own competition night
customer.target: Owners and managers of gaming cafés, pool halls, snooker parlours, PlayStation/console lounges and board-game cafés in Indian cities, who already run or want to run a regular competition night
customer.where: India — tier 1 and tier 2 cities (Bengaluru, Pune, Kochi, Hyderabad, Indore, Coimbatore)

segments.name: Manager running the floor (not the owner)
Community league organiser, no venue of their own

objections: I already do this on a whiteboard and it costs me nothing
A monthly fee for something I use four nights a month is hard to justify
My staff will not learn new software
Does this get more people through the door, or is it just admin?
Is this legal? It sounds like the betting apps that got banned
What happens when the internet drops mid-tournament?
I have no screen to put this on
Who pays the prize money — me?
habits: your busiest nights are Friday and Saturday and Tuesday is dead
you know your regulars by name and they ask when the next tournament is
you lost a whole evening last month to an argument about a disputed frame
you have a TV on the wall showing a muted cricket match
a sales rep calls you about software roughly once a fortnight

pitch:
# Winner Takes All — run your competition night

Software for your venue to run its own tournament night. You set up a bracket in
about a minute, your regulars join from their phones by scanning a code, and the
live bracket and running scores go up on the screen on your wall.

It keeps score for 8-ball pool and for football, so a disputed frame is settled
by what is on the screen rather than by argument. Run it as a weekly series and
it keeps a league table across the weeks, so the same people come back next
Tuesday to defend their place.

₹1,500 a month per venue. No contract, cancel any month.

Players pay you nothing through the software and stake nothing on the app. Entry
is free, or you collect it at the counter in your own name, exactly as you do
now. Any prize is yours or a sponsor's to give. The app never touches your
customers' money, which is what keeps it clear of the 2025 online money gaming
rules.

First month free. If your regulars do not come back for a second week, you do
not pay.
